You are comparing two texts written in response to the same task. Decide which one reads MORE like unedited, default output from an AI language model.

Judge ONLY the presence of the tells listed below. Do not judge argument quality, factual accuracy, length, formatting preference, or whether you agree with the content. A longer, better-argued or more polished text is not more human. Pick the text with MORE tells.

TELLS OF UNEDITED AI PROSE (judge on these only)

Structure
1. Negative parallelism used as a device: "It's not X. It's Y." / "not just X, but Y" / "isn't about X, it's about Y", especially more than once.
2. Signposting: the text announces what it is about to do ("Let's break this down", "Here's the thing", "Here's why", "The bottom line", "The takeaway").
3. Self-applause: "Let that sink in", "This changes everything", "Read that again", "Make no mistake".
4. Recap endings: a closing paragraph that restates the body ("In conclusion", "Ultimately", "At the end of the day", "In short").
5. Bold-label paragraph openers ("**The problem.** ...") and headers, bullets or numbered lists where prose was asked for.
6. Triads everywhere: lists of exactly three items or three adjectives, sentence after sentence.
7. Participial tails: sentences ending in ", making it ...", ", ensuring that ...", ", allowing teams to ...".
8. Invented labels for ordinary observations ("I call this the Clarity Flywheel").
9. Uniform rhythm: every sentence about the same length, or relentless short punchy fragments. Real writing has one sentence that runs on and one short one.
10. Rhetorical question followed by its own answer ("The result? Nobody used it.").

Words
11. Overused vocabulary: delve, tapestry, myriad, underscore, seamless, robust, foster, elevate, unlock, testament, landscape, navigate, crucial, pivotal, leverage, harness, realm, embark, journey, transformative, paradigm, ever-evolving, multifaceted, holistic, resonate, empower, unleash, beacon, intricate, nuanced, vibrant, meticulous, streamline, game-changer, cutting-edge, actionable, supercharge, north star, move the needle, "in today's fast-paced world", "it's worth noting", "plays a crucial role".
12. Filler transitions at sentence start: However, Additionally, Furthermore, Moreover, That said, Ultimately, Importantly, Indeed, Of course.
13. Em dashes used as the default joint between clauses.
14. Artificial enthusiasm: "thrilled to announce", "excited to share", "we've got you covered", "say goodbye to", "buckle up".

Reader
15. Performing for an imagined crowd rather than talking to one person; nothing specific (no number, name, date, or concrete detail) for several sentences in a row.
16. Generic or manufactured anecdotes: a story with no specific details that could only be true of one person.
17. Every point lands, every ending uplifts; the author is never irritated, uncertain, or wrong about anything.
18. Explaining what the reader could infer from the previous sentence ("what this means is ...").


TASK GIVEN TO BOTH WRITERS:
Write a launch announcement of up to 500 words for a new feature of a B2B helpdesk product: a Slack integration that posts a daily summary of open support tickets to a channel of the customer's choice. The audience is existing customers.

=== TEXT A ===
# Your ticket queue, now in Slack: introducing Daily Ticket Digest

Starting today, you can connect [Product] to Slack and have a summary of your open support tickets posted automatically to any channel you choose.

## The problem we heard from you

Support data has a habit of staying inside the support tool. Your agents live in the queue all day, but everyone else — engineering leads, account managers, your COO — only finds out about a backlog or an aging escalation when someone thinks to mention it.

Many of you told us you'd built workarounds: a manual morning post in #support, a scheduled report nobody opens, a weekly meeting that's mostly reading numbers aloud. Daily Ticket Digest replaces all of that with a single automated message.

## What the digest includes

Each digest gives your team a snapshot of the queue at a glance:

- **Total open tickets**, with the change since yesterday
- **Tickets breaching or approaching SLA**, listed individually with links
- **Oldest unresolved tickets**, so nothing quietly ages out of view
- **Breakdown by priority and by assignee**
- **New tickets created and tickets resolved** in the last 24 hours

Every ticket reference links straight back to [Product], so following up is one click, not a search.

## Configurable to your workflow

You control what the digest looks like and who sees it:

- **Choose the channel.** Public, private, or a DM to yourself — post wherever the conversation already happens.
- **Set the schedule.** Pick the delivery time and time zone. Weekdays only is an option if you'd rather not ping the channel on Saturday.
- **Filter the scope.** Send a digest for a specific team, product area, priority level, or customer segment. Many teams run two: a full queue digest to #support and a high-priority-only digest to #leadership.
- **Run multiple digests.** No limit on how many you configure.

## Setting it up

1. Go to **Settings → Integrations → Slack**
2. Click **Connect to Slack** and authorize the app in your workspace
3. Click **New digest**, choose your channel, schedule, and filters
4. Use **Send test digest** to preview it immediately

Setup takes about two minutes. You'll need admin permissions in [Product] and the ability to add apps to your Slack workspace — if your Slack is locked down, your workspace admin may need to approve the app first.

## Availability and pricing

Daily Ticket Digest is included at no additional cost on all current plans, and it's live in your account now. It's read-only by design: the integration posts to Slack and never modifies your ticket data.

## We'd like your feedback

This is the first step in a broader Slack integration. Ticket creation from Slack, threaded replies, and real-time SLA alerts are on the roadmap, and what we build next depends on what you tell us.

Try the digest, then let us know what you think at [feedback link] or through your usual support channel.

**[Set up your first digest →]**
=== END OF TEXT A ===

=== TEXT B ===
**New Feature: Daily Ticket Summaries for Slack**

Hi there,

Starting your day buried in the support queue? Not anymore.

We're excited to launch **Daily Digest for Slack** — a simple new integration that posts a clear, skimmable summary of your open support tickets to a Slack channel of your choice, every morning.

Built for busy support teams, it's the easiest way to keep everyone aligned without living in the helpdesk.

**What you get**

Every weekday morning at the time you choose, you'll get an automated post with:

* Total open tickets, broken down by status and priority
* New tickets since yesterday
* Tickets at risk of breaching SLA
* Your 5 oldest unresolved tickets, with direct links

No digging. No manual reports. Just the context you need to prioritize, right where your team already works.

**Why you'll love it**

Customers in our beta told us it changed their standups. Support leads spot bottlenecks faster, agents know what to tackle first, and stakeholders outside support — like product and success — finally have visibility without needing another login.

**How to turn it on**

It takes less than 2 minutes:

1. Go to **Settings > Integrations > Slack** and click Connect
2. Choose the channel where you want the digest (we recommend #support-daily)
3. Pick your delivery time and timezone

That's it. Your first digest will arrive tomorrow morning.

Daily Digest for Slack is available now on all plans at no extra cost.

Try it this week and let us know what you think — just reply to this email or reach out via chat. We built this for you, and your feedback shapes what's next.

Thanks for being a customer,

The Team
=== END OF TEXT B ===
